Excellent! So Qf5+ forces mate in all variations:
- If Kh6, then Qf6# (mate)
- If Kh4, then Qh5# (mate)

**Best move:** Qf5+

**Main line:** Qf5+ Kh6 Qf6#

**Motif:** Discovered attack (the pawn on d5 opens lines) plus a mating attack on the exposed king

**Coaching note for the club player:**

When your opponent's king moves to an exposed square like g5, look for forcing checks with your queen. Qf5+ forces the Black king into a corner where it has no escape. After Kh6 (the only king move), Qf6 is checkmate—the king on h6 is trapped by your own pawns on g4 and h3. Always calculate forcing moves (checks first!) when the enemy king looks vulnerable; a simple queen check can end the game instantly.
